tool.name: mash triangle

regex.description: An input sketch does not match the k-mer size or sketching parameters and was skipped

tool.command: @SAFE_NAME_HELPERS@ ## mash labels whole-file entries by the path it was given, so link each input under its ## Galaxy identifier; mash only recognises sketches by their .msh suffix #set $used = set() #set $links = [] #set $sketch_first = False #set $has_sequences = False #if str($inputs.input_mode) == 'collection' #set $input_files = $inputs.input_collection #else #set $input_files = $inputs.input_datasets #end if #for $input in $input_files #set $base = $safe_name($input.element_identifier) ## stay under the 255-byte filename limit with room for the collision and .msh suffixes #set $base = $base.encode('utf-8')[:200].decode('utf-8', 'ignore') #if $input.ext == 'msh' #if not $links #set $sketch_first = True #end if #set $suffix = '.msh' #if $base.endswith('.msh') #set $base = $base[:-4] #end if #else #set $has_sequences = True #set $suffix = '' #if $base.endswith('.msh') #set $base = $base + '_' #end if #end if #set $link = $base + $suffix #set $n = 1 #while $link in $used #set $link = $base + '_' + str($n) + $suffix #set $n += 1 #end while #silent $used.add($link) #silent $links.append($link) ln -s '$input' '$link' && #end for ## mash takes every sketching setting, including -i, from a leading sketch and ignores the form, ## and nothing in the form can check the input order #if $sketch_first and $has_sequences echo 'The first input is a sketch, so mash would apply its k-mer size, seed, sketch size and individual-sequence setting to the sequence inputs and ignore the settings in this form. Put a sequence dataset first, or sketch every input with the same settings.' >&2 && exit 1 && #end if ## with one input mash compares the records inside it, which for a read set means every read against every other #if str($reads_assembly.reads_assembly_selector) == 'reads' and len($links) == 1 and $has_sequences echo 'Reads mode needs at least two read datasets. With a single input mash would compare every read against every other read.' >&2 && exit 1 && #end if mash triangle -p \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} -k $kmer_size -s $sketch_size -S $seed #if str($reads_assembly.reads_assembly_selector) == 'reads': -r -m $reads_assembly.minimum_kmer_copies #if $reads_assembly.target_coverage: -c $reads_assembly.target_coverage #end if #if $reads_assembly.genome_size: -g $reads_assembly.genome_size #end if #else $reads_assembly.individual_sequences #end if #if str($output_type.output_type_selector) == 'edge': -E -v $output_type.pvalue -d $output_type.distance #end if #for $link in $links '$link' #end for > '$output'

param.label: Sequences or sketches to compare
param.help: Each dataset is compared as a whole and labelled with its dataset name

param.name: input_collection
param.label: Sequences or sketches to compare
param.help: Each element is compared as a whole and labelled with its element identifier

param.name: individual_sequences
param.label: Compare individual sequences
param.help: Compare every sequence (e.g. contig or chromosome) rather than whole datasets. Labels are then the sequence IDs from the FASTA headers.

param.name: minimum_kmer_copies
param.label: Minimum copies of each k-mer required to pass noise filter

param.name: target_coverage
param.label: Target coverage
param.help: If specified, sketching will conclude if this coverage is reached before the end of the input file (estimated by average k-mer multiplicity)

param.name: genome_size
param.label: Genome size
param.help: If specified, will be used for p-value calculation instead of an estimated size from k-mer content

param.label: K-mer size
param.help: Used to sketch sequence inputs; any sketch (msh) inputs must have been built with the same k-mer size

param.label: Sketch size
param.help: Each sketch will have at most this many non-redundant min-hashes

tool.help:
**What it does**
Estimates the Mash distance between every pair of inputs and reports the results either as a lower-triangular distance matrix or as an edge list. Inputs can be FASTA or FASTQ (gzipped or not) or Mash sketches (msh), selected as several datasets or as a list collection.
By default each dataset is sketched and compared as a whole, and is labelled in the output with its dataset name, or its element identifier when it comes from a collection. Characters other than letters, digits, ``.``, ``-`` and ``_`` are replaced by ``_``, labels longer than 200 bytes are shortened, and a numeric suffix is added if two labels would collide.
With **Compare individual sequences** (``-i``) every sequence in every input is compared separately and labelled with its FASTA sequence ID. If only a single sequence dataset is given, mash compares its individual sequences regardless of this setting. Sequence IDs, like the names stored in sketches, are used as they are and are not made unique, so the same label can appear more than once, for example when the assemblies all name their contigs ``contig00001`` and so on.
Sketch (msh) inputs are labelled with the names stored in the sketch when it was built, not with their Galaxy dataset name, and keep the settings they were built with. Each sketch must have been built with the k-mer size and seed set here; the job fails if a sketch does not match, rather than silently leaving it out of the result. When sketches are mixed with sequence datasets the first input must be a sequence dataset: mash would otherwise take the k-mer size, seed, sketch size and individual-sequence setting from the first sketch and ignore this form, so the job fails instead. If every input is a sketch, the first one sets the parameters and the others must match it.
**Reads** mode (``-r``) filters out low-copy k-mers that are likely to be sequencing errors, as in **mash sketch**. It needs at least two inputs; a single read dataset would otherwise be split into a comparison of every read against every other read, so the job fails instead.
**Output**
*Lower-triangular distance matrix* (relaxed Phylip). The first line holds the number of entries, then each row holds a label followed by its distances to all entries above it::
3 sample_A sample_B 0.00960897 sample_C 0.0556462 0.0659724
*Edge list* (tab-separated, no header). One line per pair with the columns ``seq1``, ``seq2``, ``distance``, ``p-value`` and ``shared-hashes``::
sample_B sample_A 0.00960897 0 691/1000 sample_C sample_A 0.0556462 0 184/1000 sample_C sample_B 0.0659724 0 143/1000
The edge list can be restricted to pairs below a maximum distance (``-d``) and/or p-value (``-v``).
